post.description:
Reissue an invoice with fields derived from the **current** tenant
billing config: invoice number (per current ``invoice_numbering_mode``),
due date (per current ``default_payment_terms_days`` and
``show_due_date``), and — importantly — per-line-item unit prices
refreshed from the current fee schedule.

Preserved:
- Line item rows (no add/delete), including manual line items.
- ``created_at`` timestamp, ``incident_id``, ``status``,
  ``billed_to_*`` overrides, notes.

Rate refresh policy:
- Auto-sourced line items (``source`` != MANUAL) are matched back
  to the current fee schedule by ``description == FeeScheduleItem.label``.
  If a match is found, ``unit_price`` + ``unit`` update from the
  current ``default_rate`` + ``display_unit_label``. This is the
  whole point of regenerate — pick up the $0.005/gal fix after a
  schedule edit.
- Manual line items are left untouched. Chief-edited rows aren't
  owned by a schedule row.
- Orphaned auto rows (description no longer matches any fee row)
  stay at their recorded unit_price. Flagged in the audit event
  so ops can reconcile.

VOID records cannot regenerate (terminal state).

A supplementary audit event is written directly via
``enqueue_audit`` with before/after snapshots (number, subtotal,
total, per-line-item unit_price deltas). The standard middleware
audit also captures the POST, but this custom event carries the
diff a forensic reviewer would actually want.

so an organization-scoped board refetched less often and then
displayed every agency's responders anyway. Resolving the caller's
organization here is what makes the setting actually narrow what a
board shows. Tenant-wide remains the default and the fallback for
an unattributable login, so a misconfiguration degrades to today's
behaviour rather than blanking a board.

post.description:
Partial-success batch persist of self-reported locations.

The typical caller is the Rally PWA flushing its offline
queue after reconnect — many samples, some possibly invalid
(out-of-range coords from a buggy queue entry, timestamps
from a clock that drifted while offline). Persist what's
valid; report the failures by index so the client can drop
them and stop replaying.

Validation is per-item and runs in the controller (the
per-item schema deliberately has no Pydantic field
constraints — see ``PersonnelSelfBatchLocationItem``):

- ``-90 ≤ latitude ≤ 90``
- ``-180 ≤ longitude ≤ 180``
- ``accuracy ≥ 0`` when present
- ``captured_at`` within +2 minutes future / -7 days past
  (looser than the single endpoint's -24 hours to
  accommodate honest offline flush — multi-day offline
  shifts are legitimately aged but anything past a week
  almost certainly indicates a client-side queue bug)

Every persisted sample is attributed to the JWT principal's
``user_id``. There is no field on the per-item schema for
any identity, so the wire shape cannot influence
attribution. The previous ``NoPersonnelMapping`` 422 path
has been removed — Rally location is User-keyed and does
not require a Personnel link.

Returns ``201`` with ``{"created": N, "rejected":
[{"index": i, "reason": "..."}, ...]}``. Empty ``rejected``
means the whole batch landed; ``created = 0`` with a full
``rejected`` list means nothing landed but the response is
still a 201 (the batch was accepted; its items weren't).
